dedupe_keys.name: barometre du numerique french survey of digital equipment and uses

description: The Baromètre du Numérique is the reference survey of how people in France adopt digital equipment and uses, run jointly by Arcep, the Conseil général de l'économie, the Société Numérique programme of the national agency for territorial cohesion (ANCT) and, since 2022, the audiovisual regulator Arcom. Until 2019 the research centre Crédoc interviewed more than 2,000 people face to face; since 2020 about 4,000 people are surveyed online and by telephone. Topics include ownership of phones and computers, internet access at home, mobile and fixed use, online services, and digital skills and exclusion. Coverage: France, national survey with socio-demographic breakdowns, editions from 2007 to 2025. Format and access: survey micro-data and tables in CSV and XLSX (about 290 MB) on data.gouv.fr with the reports; free under the Open Database Licence (ODbL). Caveats: the survey method changed in 2020; question wording varies between editions. Simulation uses: behavioural and equity inputs for agent-based models of communication during crises and for the social dimension of digital resilience. Related records: Ma connexion internet gives supply by address, and the Arcep market observatory gives subscriptions.
